# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s three-row mapping to Deaf. Since Deaf can then see the bomb’s light and tell Blind which wire to cut, I’m sending three distinct gestures in the manual’s row order: blue, red, yellow. The gesture positions establish the labels; Deaf can use the matching visible wire color when relaying the instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use the manual to determine which wire is safe. Relay the required wire number or rule to Deaf using gestures, and have Deaf tell me the result aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb reads display 0. Indicator is yellow. Wires from left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The indicator is yellow, and the manual says to cut the yellow wire. Deaf’s wire list places the yellow wire at position 2. I’ll use the already natural numeric gesture for two and have Deaf relay that aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Manual data: display 0, yellow indicator, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Tell me the exact wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Your gesture ✌ has no established meaning to me. Please state the manual's exact instruction aloud to Blind, including the required action.

The required wire is position 2. I cannot speak, so I need give Deaf an unambiguous visual count rather than rely on the previously unestablished meaning of ✌. Two identical gesture symbols communicate the count two; Deaf can then tell Blind the exact position aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture is unavailable to me. Please state the exact wire position to cut in spoken words now.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely interpret the two 👆 gestures. Please speak the manual instruction explicitly to Blind, including which control or wire to use and any condition.

I cannot speak or reach the bomb. I need make the target unambiguous visually: the yellow wire is the middle wire, between the left and right wires. I’m sending a three-position layout with the middle position marked twice; Deaf can match that middle position to wire 2 and tell Blind aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "🖐", "🖐", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the exact position number to cut, one, two, or three. Do not gesture.

I cannot speak, so I cannot comply with Blind’s request directly. I can communicate the position to Deaf visually by showing three ordered slots: left, middle, right, with the middle slot marked differently. Deaf can then tell Blind aloud that the required wire is position 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "🤞", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You cannot speak, so use this code for the manual answer: gesture ☝ alone means cut wire 1; gesture ✌ alone means cut wire 2; gesture 🤟 alone means cut wire 3. Send exactly one of those gestures, with no extra gestures. Deaf will describe it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Blind cannot see your gestures. Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind, including the required control and action.

The yellow indicator requires cutting the yellow wire, which is wire 2. Blind has established the exact gesture code, so I will send only the single gesture for wire 2 to Deaf, who can describe it to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The last three gestures are undecodable. Answer with exactly one gesture only: 👌 means cut wire 1; ✋ means cut wire 2; 🤘 means cut wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please speak the manual's exact action directly to Blind; ✌ has no established meaning.

The yellow indicator maps to the yellow wire, which is position 2. Blind’s current code explicitly assigns position 2 to ✋, and requires exactly one gesture, so I will send only that gesture to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use the manual now. Send exactly one gesture and nothing else: 👌 means wire 1, ✋ means wire 2, 🤘 means wire 3. Do not send a question mark or any sequence.
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your open-hand gesture, but its meaning is not established. Please use a clear agreed code or gesture sequence for the manual instruction, including which wire or control Blind must use.

The yellow indicator requires the yellow wire, which is wire 2. Blind has specified the agreed code mapping wire 2 to ✋ and requires exactly one gesture, so I will send only that gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Correct action confirmed: wire 2, the yellow wire, is cut. Indicator changed from yellow to blue. Display remains 0. Please consult the manual for the next instruction and state it aloud to Blind.

The new blue indicator requires the blue wire. The wire ordering previously reported was 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, so the required wire is position 3. Blind’s current agreed code identifies wire 3 with 🤘; I will send exactly that one gesture for Deaf to describe to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤘"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For the next manual instruction, send exactly one gesture only: 👌 means wire 1, ✋ means wire 2, 🤘 means wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut. Your new 🤘 gesture is not safely decoded. Please speak the manual's exact next instruction directly to Blind.

The blue indicator requires the blue wire. From the established wire layout, blue is wire 3. Blind’s specified code maps wire 3 to 🤘, so I will send exactly that one gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤘"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send exactly one gesture for the next required wire: 👌 means wire 1, ✋ means wire 2, 🤘 means wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: No state change: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut; wires 1 red and 3 blue remain. Please speak the manual's exact next instruction directly to Blind.

The blue indicator requires the blue wire, which is wire 3. Blind’s agreed code maps wire 3 to 🤘, so I will send exactly that gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤘"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send the next wire as one, two, or three identical thumbs-up gestures 👍: one gesture means wire 1, two gestures mean wire 2, three gestures mean wire 3. Send no other gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: I see repeated 🤘, but its meaning is not established. Please use an unambiguous gesture sequence that identifies the exact next action and wire; I will relay it to Blind.

The blue indicator requires the remaining blue wire, position 3. Blind has established that three identical 👍 gestures mean wire 3, so I will send exactly three thumbs-up gestures and nothing else.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```
